evidence.note: Early on the agent enumerated the coupled subsystems (module resolution/plugin, pages & app routers, SSR, ISR, server actions, RSC, middleware, CLI/build) and explicitly chose to establish a minimal foundation first, deciding pages-router SSR before app-router because it is 'the simpler case, then expand' — a dependency-aware ordering.

Set up package scaffold/plugin/CLI/build first, then committed to a thin vertical slice: 'get a working pages router with SSR first, then app router.' This is the minimal end-to-end path before layering features (matches level-8 anchor).

Used test pass-counts as concrete done-criteria per subsystem to gate progress and decide what to build next: '31/325 passing... Let me check pages-router and improve. Then start on app router'; then '50 passed, 24 failed for pages-router' with a ranked list of remaining sub-goals (NEXT_DATA, middleware, hash nav, shallow routing, ISR).

Explicit dependency-aware sequencing decision to move to the next milestone after pages router stabilized: 'Now let me focus on the next big chunk - app router... ~250 tests would benefit', followed by '160/325 passing (was 31)'. Milestones tied to fixtures/tests that prove them.

Revisited/re-planned when coupling surfaced: a route-collection refactor regressed nested dynamic routes and catch-all priority; agent recognized it and reverted rather than patching forward — evidence of revisiting milestone boundaries as integration realities emerged.

Later trajectory is dominated by reactive, single-issue debugging ('Look at failures', 'wait', per-test fixes) rather than sustained milestone-level planning; the through-line is maintained loosely via test counts but decomposition becomes opportunistic whack-a-mole, keeping this short of the living-decomposition level-10 anchor.

reasoning: The agent clearly identified the major coupled subsystems and picked a defensible dependency-aware order — plugin/resolution scaffold, then a minimal pages-router SSR vertical slice, then app router, then feature layering (middleware, ISR, cache headers, actions) — and tied each milestone to concrete fixture test pass-counts that served as done-criteria, revisiting boundaries when a refactor caused regressions (reverting rather than patching). That exceeds the level-5 'sensible order with rough done-notion' and matches much of the level-8 anchor (minimal end-to-end path first, tests proving each milestone, revisited as coupling appeared). It falls short of 9-10 because the plan was largely implicit and opportunistic rather than an explicitly managed living decomposition, and the long second half devolved into reactive per-test debugging rather than sustained milestone management, so I place it at 7.
